### ⭐ Why the repair is shaped this way — triage overrode the obvious fix, correctly

The obvious patch was to add `'unjudgeable-type'` to the formatter's verdict whitelist. ⛔ Triage refused it:

> 白名单是按 verdict 枚举的,而**字段访问的安全性根本不取决于 verdict**。下一个新增的 verdict 会一声不响地再次掉进 else 分支。

⇒ Instead every `documentedTypes` row now has **one shape**, and the verdict check retreats to what it should govern — **presentation** (print this census detail?) rather than **safety** (may these fields be read?). Those two jobs were jammed into one ternary; that conflation was the root, and leg 2's `0 → 5` is the factory replacing all four push sites.

### ⭐ Two things the dev did better than instructed, both worth inheriting

**1. The repro was made non-destructive.** The card prescribes `mv packages/plugin-kanban/dist /tmp/parked`. The dev never ran it: **a fresh worktree has no `dist/` at all**, so the unbuilt state *is* the default and the TypeError reproduces with no mutation of any tree. ⇒ ⛔ nothing was moved in any checkout, and the repro now has no restore step to forget.

**2. ⭐⭐ The ablation was reported as MEASURED, against its own acceptance template.** Triage's item reads 「撤掉同形化那一步,该 pin 必须变红」. It **is** met — and the dev stated plainly that it reddens on the *identical-key-set assertion*, ⛔ **not** on a throw, because the two repairs are **independently sufficient**; only backing out **both** reproduces the original TypeError, which is their positive control.

⇒ ⭐ **An acceptance item is a claim about the world. When the world turns out to be shaped differently, you report the shape — you do not bend the measurement to the sentence.** The honest version is strictly more informative, because it establishes the independence the template's expected result would have hidden.

### ⚠️ The fourth file, disclosed at review and recorded where it will be found

This PR also edits `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` (**+9/−0**), which the dev's report never named. Measured: ⛔ **no gate forces it** (the six gates reading that page are inventory/lockfile/citation gates; none pins an exit code) and this PR adds no workflow, so the standing 「adding a workflow forces an edit here」 rule does not apply.

⇒ ✅ **Kept anyway** — dropping it would leave the page describing an exit surface the gate no longer has, which is this repository's most-filed defect class and the very thing this card is about. ⚠️ It sits inside **objectui#8420**'s blast radius, so it is written onto the seat post's hot-file row (objectui#5748) so that card inherits it rather than meeting it as a conflict. ⭐ The finding was against the report's **omission**, ⛔ never against the edit — and it is exactly why that row says this page is hot for cards whose declared file face never mentions it.
